title: Mocking and Test Doubles
learning_outcomes: Explain the central rule or purpose of mocking and test doubles using at least one correct term from the lesson.
Interpret or adapt a small Kotlin example that demonstrates mocking and test doubles.
Identify one relevant edge case, debugging step, or version/platform constraint.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will learn **Mocking and Test Doubles** as part of **Testing, Debugging, Documentation, and Quality**. Reliable Kotlin code is supported by repeatable tests, meaningful assertions, debuggable failure reports, documentation, and review—not by coverage alone. Use the subtopics—Stubs, Fakes, and Mocks, Isolating Collaborators, When Not to Mock—as a checklist: predict what the example will do, then verify it in a project configured for the target platform.
content.why_it_matters: Professional applications need repeatable tests, clear APIs, dependable dependencies, security checks, and observable failures. Apply this concept in small steps before integrating it into a larger project.

content_blocks.title: Troubleshooting and reset

Read the first useful compiler or runtime message, check imports and declared dependencies, reduce the example to a minimal case, and rerun. For target-specific code, use the target toolchain rather than assuming a console or browser runner can execute it.
